transcript:
This message comes from Angie. Angie has been helping homeowners find skilled
pros to get their home projects done well for over 30 years. For everything from minor repairs
to major remodels, find reviews, pricing, and booking at Angie.com or on the Angie app.
This is NPR News Now. The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in New York City, I'm Dua Lisa Kautau. A historic town hall in France,
more than 140 years old, has largely burnt today, casting a shot on mostly peaceful student protests
across the country. Cars were also set on fire and stores sacked and pillaged in many cities.
NPR's Eleanor Beersley reports even protesters have condemned the violence,
saying it takes away from their valid cause.
The main protest march in Paris was peaceful, but all around were pockets of violence that
police were unable to control. 65-year-old protester Pascal Ordeuxu came out to march
in support of his daughter, a teacher, and his grandkids, who are students. He says the
media loves to show the violence. It's nothing compared to what people are fighting for, he says,
and focusing on it lets the government off the hook. But TV footage showed a different story.
Some 1,200 people have been arrested and hooded youths clashed with police well into the evening.
Far left leaders who joined the protesters distanced themselves from the violence,
saying a legitimate march had been infiltrated by troublemakers.
Eleanor Beersley, NPR News, Paris.
President Trump was in Kentucky today visiting one of many states he won in
2024. He's hoping to give Republican candidates a boost just weeks before the midterms.
From member station WVXU in Cincinnati, Zach Karyan reports.
Trump downplayed the impact of rising costs and again promised benefits if Republicans beat out
Democrats this November. If the Republicans win, you'll each have $5,000 in your pocket and
economic success for our country like we have never seen before. Trump told the crowd he expects
candidates he's backed in Kentucky to win easily, but says other races will be close,
like the Senate face-off between Ohio Republican incumbent John Husted and Democrat and former
Senator Sherrod Brown. For NPR News, I'm Zach Karyan in Highland Heights, Kentucky.
Oregon's Governor Tina Kotak says it will be days before any information on the school
shooting that killed three children and their teacher in Bent, Oregon is released to the public.
Police today identified the 25-year-old educator as Megan Lambert.
I did have a chance to talk to the mother of Megan Lambert and
obviously they are heartbroken. Megan was an amazing teacher and volleyball coach,
loved in the community and you know we have to remember that these events have so much ripple
effect across the community. The governor, a Democrat, is seeking another four years in office.
Her challenger is Republican State Senator Christine Drazin.
Hurricane Trudy is approaching Mexico's coast, possibly bringing four to eight inches. This is NPR.
Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelensky says the U.S. is working to set up a trilateral meeting
with Russia to end the fighting between Moscow and cave. This comes just hours after President
Trump signed an executive order to temporarily pause sanctions against Russia. Meanwhile,
in Ukraine's capital, the Kyiv Independent reports protesters demanded that the mayor
of Kyiv resign over what some claim is his failure to prepare for the incoming winter
as energy infrastructure continued to be targeted by Russia.
The Golden State Valkyries beat the Atlanta Dream '68 to '64 in Game 1, the WNBA Finals,
from member station KALW Jordan Carnes reports. Saturday's game marked the Valkyries' first
appearance in the finals, while the Dream's last visit was in 2013. Both teams surprised the league
with dominant playoff runs, each sweeping the former consecutive champs, the Aces and the Liberty
in the semifinals. Game 1 was marked by defense. The Valkyries are the top-ranked defensive team
in the league, while the Dream's Angel Reiss was named Defensive Player of the Year. However,
it wasn't enough to beat the Valkyries on their home turf, Ballhala, which has sold out every
game in its two years. Game 2 of the Best of Seven series will be on Monday in San Francisco.
For NPR News, I'm Jordan Carnes.
In the Pacific, super typhoon Champi is strengthening and moving toward the U.S.
territory of Guam, with maximum sustained winds of 140 miles per hour. I'm Dua Halisa Ekowta, NPR News,
in New York City.
Iowans, you can register to vote at any time. Election Day is Tuesday, November 3rd.
Sponsored by Civic Futures Fund.

topics.text: Historic town hall in France burns during nationwide student protests with violence in several cities
Trump campaigns in Kentucky, promising $5,000 payments if Republicans win the midterms
Oregon governor says school shooting details will take days; teacher Megan Lambert identified as victim
Hurricane Trudy approaches Mexico's coast, possibly bringing four to eight inches of rain
Zelensky says US working to set up trilateral meeting with Russia after Trump pauses Russia sanctions
Kyiv protesters demand mayor resign over winter preparations amid Russian energy infrastructure attacks
Golden State Valkyries beat Atlanta Dream 68-64 in WNBA Finals Game 1
Super Typhoon Champi strengthens with 140 mph winds, moving toward Guam
